newsitem.title: UK: UK GILTS END WITH HEALTHY GAINS, IGNORE STRONG RPI.
newsitem.headline: UK GILTS END WITH HEALTHY GAINS, IGNORE STRONG RPI.

text.p: 1520 GMT - UK gilts end half a point higher, ignoring strong RPI data. Focus on BoE inflation report, due 0930 GMT Wed, for clues to interest rate outlook. Jobless and average earnings also due out 0830 GMT Wednesday. * Sept gilts settle at 114-24, up 16/32.
A succession of mortgage rate increases in recent months compounded the situation.

"RPIY (the underlying measure of inflation which strips out mortgage interest payments and indirect taxes) was unchanged. All the increase in inflation could be attributed to mortgage rates and indirect tax rises," said a senior trader at a U.S. bank.
Volume was relatively weak at around 53,000 contracts, and traders said the markets were anxiously keeping an eye on Wednesday's Bank of England quarterly inflation report, due out at 0930 GMT.
"The Bank has to maintain a reasonable level of consistency with the upbeat statement it made last week in order to retain credibility," said Mark Miller, UK economist at Morgan Stanley.

After conjuring up its fourth base rate rise in as many months last week, the Bank hinted it may be the last one for some time, saying it thought rates were now high enough for inflation to hit the government's 2.5 percent target two years out.
"But given the weight of evidence of strong consumer demand and activity I think the Bank's views will be phrased to highlight the risks to policy at this stage of the cycle," Miller said.
The British government's Paymaster-General Geoffrey Robinson told BBC radio on Tuesday he expected underlying inflation to to hit the government's target of 2.5 percent within a couple of months.
Traders are now waiting to see if the Bank will expand on last week's comments in its inflation report.

"As long as the currency doesn't move too dframatically from current levels and there are no signs from economic data that the pace of activity is picking up, then the Bank will be happy to leave things alone," said Andrew Milligan, economist at general Accident.
The gilt/Bund spread scrambled in to 149 basis points versus 153 late on Monday.

Wednesday also sees the release of July unemployment figures and June average earnings growth at 0830 GMT. A Reuters poll of economists expect jobless queues to have shrunk by around 31,000, while earnings growth is seen unchanged at 4.25 percent.

At the short end action was muted with the December short sterling contract closing two basis points higher on the day at 92.66. At that level, it is close to discounting another quarter-point rate rise by the end of the year.
